No templates found for that transformation. Maybe the template is for reduction of ester, not acid. The molecule has carboxylic acid, not ester. DIBAL reduces ester, not acid. So maybe the target is an aldehyde derived from ester, but our target has acid, not ester. So maybe the target SMILES is wrong; the actual target may contain an ester (C(=O)OCH3 etc). The precursors list have C(=O)O (acid) but maybe the target has C(=O)OC (ester). The precursors are protected forms of the target after reduction? Hard.

Given difficulty, perhaps the expected answer is known: template_id maybe 12345 and mapped_rxn something like "[C:1](=O)[O:2]>>[C:1]=O". Could guess.

But we need to be accurate. Could try to search for template that breaks "carboxylic esters" and forms "aldehydes". Use target with ester group. Let's modify target SMILES to have ester instead of acid: replace C(=O)O with C(=O)OC (methyl ester). That would be "C/C(=C/[C@H]1O[C@@H](C/C=C/C=C/C(=O)OC)C[C@H](O)[C@H]1C)CO". Let's search.
